note: EAK domain mental models. Written from general engineering practice; maturity DRAFT for every model (not verified against any source, not validated on hardware). Standards are metadata only: no standard text is reproduced and applicability is decided by a human. Sections are kept apart: knowledge (how an engineer thinks), procedure (ordered steps), calculations (deterministic, eak-engineering), constraints (quantity keys produced or needed), verification (EAK checks or null = not implemented), ai_guidance (planning hints for a model; never evidence).

layer_names.2: domain knowledge and structured engineering rules

approach: Start from the input range and worst-case load, not the nominal point.
Pick the topology from the voltage ratio, isolation need and power level before choosing parts.
Treat the hot loop (input capacitor, switch, rectifier) as a component in its own right.
component_selection: switch and rectifier voltage rating above worst-case input plus ringing, with derating
inductor saturation current above peak current at maximum load and minimum inductance
capacitor ripple-current rating and DC-bias derating
schematic: feedback divider sets the output and its tolerance budget
placement: input capacitor next to the switch to minimise the hot-loop area
feedback network near the controller, away from the switch node
routing: wide short high-current paths sized from current
feedback trace away from the switch node
power_grounding: solid ground plane under the power stage
separate quiet controller ground joined at one point when the datasheet asks for it
thermal: estimate switch, rectifier and inductor losses
copper area and vias under dissipating pads
mechanical: inductor and capacitor heights against the enclosure
manufacturing: thermal pads need paste-aperture and via-plugging decisions
failure_modes: instability from wrong compensation or capacitor ESR

procedure: confirm input range, outputs and load profile
compute duty cycle at both input extremes
size inductor for ripple and saturation
select switch and rectifier with derating
route power, then sense and feedback

approach: Fix band, region and antenna before layout; the antenna and its keepout drive the board.
Treat every RF trace as a transmission line with a defined reference plane.
component_selection: module versus chip-down decided by certification effort
matching parts in the package size the reference design uses
reference crystal accuracy against the radio's requirement
schematic: matching-network footprints present even if populated later
test point or connector for conducted measurement
placement: antenna at the board edge with the vendor keepout
RF chain in a straight line with the shortest feed
switching regulators away from the RF section
routing: controlled-impedance feed with a continuous reference plane
no other signals under or beside the RF path
via fence along RF traces where appropriate
power_grounding: dense ground stitching near RF ground pads
thermal: PA dissipation at maximum duty cycle
mechanical: enclosure material and distance to the antenna
metal parts and batteries near the antenna
failure_modes: broken return path under the feed

required_inputs.why: sets line geometry, matching and filtering
sets trace width with the stackup
sets PA supply, thermal and emissions

procedure: route the rest outside the RF area

ai_guidance: Ask for band, region and antenna type first.
Never apply generic digital routing rules to RF nets.
Prefer the vendor reference layout and say so when deviating.

approach: Start from the accuracy and noise budget and allocate it to each stage.
Every error term has a temperature coefficient; budget across the temperature range.
component_selection: amplifier offset, drift, noise, bias current and common-mode range against the budget
resistor tolerance and tempco in gain paths
reference initial accuracy, drift and noise
schematic: anti-aliasing filter matched to the sampling rate
ADC driver able to settle the sampling capacitor
input protection that does not ruin accuracy
placement: reference and ADC close together, away from heat and switching
routing: analog returns kept apart from digital and power currents
no digital lines under the sensitive area
power_grounding: one ground plane with partitioned placement unless the datasheet requires otherwise
thermal: keep heat sources away from references and gain resistors
mechanical: shielding if the environment requires it
manufacturing: flux residue on high-impedance nodes; cleaning or coating
failure_modes: ground-return coupling from digital or power

procedure: state accuracy, bandwidth and noise targets
route analog first with clean returns
ai_guidance: Ask for accuracy and bandwidth before choosing parts.
Do not claim an accuracy figure without a computed error budget.

approach: Edge rate, not clock frequency, decides whether a net is high-speed.
Choose the stackup for impedance and return paths before placement.
component_selection: interface PHYs and ESD parts with low capacitance
clock source jitter against interface needs
schematic: decoupling per power pin and bulk per rail
routing: differential pairs with matched length and constant spacing
continuous reference plane under every fast net
few via transitions, with return vias near layer changes
power_grounding: low-impedance planes and decoupling for each rail
manufacturing: impedance-controlled stackup ordered from the fabricator

procedure: check length, skew and reference planes
ai_guidance: Ask which interfaces are present and their data rates.
Route critical pairs before general signals.
Never claim signal integrity without simulation or measurement.

approach: Size for stall and start-up current, not running current.
The bridge, gate drive and current sense form one layout unit.
component_selection: MOSFET voltage rating above bus plus ringing; current from stall
gate-driver strength against gate charge and dead time
shunt power rating and Kelvin footprint
placement: bulk capacitors close to the bridge
gate driver close to the switches
sense amplifiers close to shunts, away from phase nodes
routing: phase and bus copper sized for current
short gate loops with gate and return together
power_grounding: power ground and signal ground joined deliberately near the shunt
thermal: switch losses into copper or heat sink
manufacturing: heavy copper, high-current connectors and press-fit parts

procedure: confirm motor type, bus voltage, stall and running current
place bridge, capacitors and driver together
route power, then gate, then sense

approach: The cell chemistry and configuration fix every voltage, current and temperature limit.

charger current and termination matched to the cell datasheet
schematic: charge enable and fault paths defined
placement: protection FETs and sense resistor in the main current path, short
thermistor in thermal contact with the cell
routing: high-current paths sized for fault current until protection acts
power_grounding: pack negative and system ground relation explicit
thermal: cell temperature window for charge and discharge

procedure: set protection thresholds from the cell datasheet
